title: onboarding-credit-hedge-scratchpad
body:
Purpose / problem statement:
- We give free credits at sign-up to drive activation. A small fraction of users consume a disproportionate share (power users + bots) and destroy gross margin before we can detect and convert them.
- Need a lightweight, product-facing "credit hedge" mechanism to reduce tail exposure while keeping activation flow frictionless.

Goals for hedge design:
- Reduce worst-case subsidy per account by ~3-5x for first 7 days without turning off product experience.
- Preserve conversion signal (i.e., let genuine testers get value).
- Make implementation cheap (feature flags + simple metering rules) and reversible.

Principles / constraints:
- Credits are a marketing budget; still need to be compelling.
- Avoid surprise billing: if we throttle, surface clear messaging.
- Prefer graduated restrictions over hard-cutoffs: throttles, rate-limits, conversion nudges.
- Must integrate with existing credit accounting (sessionized ledger) and billing triggers.

Hedge proposal (sketch):
1) Staged credit release (90/9/1 model):
   - On sign-up grant 90% of the advertised credit as "usable-immediately" but with a soft per-minute throughput cap and per-session token cap.
   - 9% of credit is "watchlist reserve": available but subject to manual/auto-review if consumed rapidly.
   - 1% small reserve for API-key tests (prevent zero-UX).
2) Dynamic decay / lock after anomalous consumption:
   - Define anomaly: >X tokens in Y minutes or >Z sessions in a day. If triggered, lock reserve and extend KYC prompt or require small payment to unlock.
3) Convertible credit coupons:
   - Allow partner/SE teams to issue convertible credits that expire slower but require an onboarding milestone (e.g., create 3 fine-tuned prompts or integrate SDK).
4) Exposure cap per account-day: logical cap = min(globalAdvertisedCredit, advertised * 2 on day1, 1.2* day2, etc.)

Back-of-envelope unit econ math (rough numbers to sanity check):
Assumptions:
- GPU throughput: 800 tokens/sec (~2.88M tokens/hr) for mid-sized model (batching).
- Effective cloud GPU cost: $3.00 / GPU-hour (on amortized reserved infra); marginal cost for hosted could be $6/hr incl infra ops. Use both cases.
- Token/sec -> token cost: if 2.88M tokens/hr and cost $3/hr => $3 / 2,880k = $0.00104 per 1k tokens (reserved infra). If $6/hr => $0.00208 per 1k tokens.
- Avg onboarding session: 350 tokens in (prompt + context) + 250 tokens out = 600 tokens per session.
- Average sessions per new user day0: optimistic 6, mid 2, bad 40 (bot/power).

Scenario A (typical):
- Day0 usage: 6 sessions * 600 tokens = 3600 tokens = 3.6k tokens => cost ~ $0.0037 (reserved) to $0.0075 (market).
- 1000 new signups in campaign => cost ~= $3.7 to $7.5 for day0 (cheap).

Scenario B (power/bot tail):
- Bad actor: 40 sessions * 600 = 24k tokens => 24k/1k * $0.00208 ~= $0.05 (market) per bad actor (still small per user). But the problem is extreme scale: 50 such accounts => $2.5.
- The real risk is when users exercise long-generation behavior or embedding-heavy flows: 1 long-run job = 500k tokens -> cost ~$1.04-$2.08 per job. 10 such users early = $10-$20.

Interpretation: 
- On a per-new-user basis the numbers look small. Why worry? Because campaigns bringing 100k signups can create observable dollar exposure; also, some workflows (embeddings, long chattiness) are orders of magnitude more expensive.
- Hedging must be focused on curbing the tail (long jobs, continuous loops) rather than micro-sessions.

Hedge knobs (quick list) with expected impact:
- Per-session token soft cap (e.g., 60k tokens/session at default) -> cuts long-job tail.
- Burst budget window (e.g., allow 10k tokens/minute and then throttle) -> reduces loops/abuse.
- Reserve gating for embedding endpoints (higher unit cost) -> require small payment or manual unlock.
- Credit decay curve: ads credits unlock 25% day0, +25% day3, +50% day7 (reduces immediate burst).

Conversion economics sanity check (simplified):
- Suppose conversion rate from trial to paid = 3% baseline.
- CAC is separate. Lifetime revenue per converted user (LTR) = $800 (ARR-style).
- If we cut subsidy by $2 per converted account (via hedge) and it increases friction by 1% absolute (3%->2%), need to check net revenue impact:
   - For 10000 trials: baseline conversions = 300 -> revenue = 300*$800 = $240k. Subsidy cost removed = 10000*$1 avg subsidy = $10k -> net +$10k.
   - If hedge causes conversions to drop to 200 -> revenue = 200*$800 = $160k -> net -$70k.
- So prioritize low-friction hedges with minimal impact to conversion funnel. Experiment!

Implementation quick plan (MVP):
- Feature flag: staged release + soft throttle + reserve gating. (Dev owner: @Samir)
- Metrics to track: subsidy per account-day, % of accounts hitting reserve, post-hedge conversion rate, false positives (manual unlocks). (Dashboard: product-hosted-api/credits-hedge)
- Phased rollout: 1000 accounts (canary), 10k accounts (beta), full.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where to store reserve state? (Billing ledger vs. ephemeral flag). Prefer ledger for auditability.
- Messaging copy for throttle/unlock (legal sign-off?).
- How to let SEs override for named accounts? Coupon-based convertibles?
- Edge case: shared API keys across accounts—how to attribute and hedge? Add heuristics by IP/UA.

Quick experiment ideas:
- A/B: 50/50 for new signups; control = current flat credit; variant = staged 90/9/1 with soft throttle. Measure subsidy, activation (first meaningful action), 7-day retention, conversion at 30/60 days.
- Blacklist heuristics: if account hits reserve unlock more than twice in 48 hours -> flag for manual review.

Notes to self:
- Keep initial caps generous; we want to avoid braking legitimate integrations. Target reducing extreme tail (embedding jobs, continuous loops).
- Discuss with SRE about cost accounting and whether we can accurately map token billing to GPU-hours in near real-time.

References/links (internal):
- Confluence: onboarding-credit-policy (linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-4521 (prototype hedge flag)
- Slack thread: pricing-threads for debate on conversion sensitivity

Action items (short):
- [ ] Samir: sketch the feature flag API and ledger changes (1 week)
- [ ] Leah: mockup UX text for throttle/upgrade flow (3 days)
- [ ] Elliot: run 1-week historic log sweep to quantify how many signups triggered long-job patterns in last Q (2 weeks)

End.
